faqs.q: Do I need a separate page for each city I serve in Quebec?
faqs.a: If you genuinely serve more than one city and can describe each one distinctly, separate pages help, because people search with a city name attached. Copied pages that only swap the place name tend to hurt more than help.

faqs.q: Do Quebec city pages risk looking duplicated?
faqs.a: Only if they are thin and swap the place name. We build each page around genuinely local detail so it stands on its own and avoids the look of doorway pages.

faqs.q: Which cities in Quebec should I target first?
faqs.a: Start with the places you already serve and can describe distinctly, often around Montreal, Quebec City, Laval, Gatineau and Longueuil. Pages for areas you genuinely cover rank faster and convert better than a page that claims the whole province.

faqs.q: Is a Quebec-wide page enough on its own?
faqs.a: Rarely. Clients search with a city or region attached, so a single provincial page misses most of the demand. A hub page plus focused city pages matches how people actually search in Quebec.

faqs.q: Do you guarantee the number one position?
faqs.a: No ethical provider can guarantee a specific position, because search results change constantly. We follow a proven process, measure the results that matter such as enquiries and booked projects, and report them transparently.
